In 1984, Ric Kayne, with the support of John Anderson, founded Kayne Anderson Capital Advisors, L.P. (“KACALP“) to manage the funds of its principals and select clients. KACALP currently manages investments principally through private investment partnerships and public closed-end funds and, as of March 31, 2022, has more than $32 billion in assets under management. KACALP is entirely owned by its investment professionals and management.

KACALP’s separately dedicated investment teams focus on generating consistent results across a variety of strategies, which include public investing in energy infrastructure and other specialized marketable securities sectors, and private investing in energy, growth capital, real estate and middle market credit.

results.name: Helikon Long Short Equity Fund
results.management_company_description:
Federico Riggio and his team deploy capital across Europe and selected Emerging Markets, with other domiciles of listing (such as US and Asia) justified by underlying economic drivers. The Helikon Long Short Equity Fund aims to deliver absolute returns over the medium term through implementing a concentrated, value-driven long/short investment strategy, with an opportunistic credit exposure. The Fund is currently hard closed and is only accepting subscriptions where there are offsetting redemptions.

The portfolio is usually built on a 2:1 equity long/short ratio. Typical high conviction long equity positions are sized at 10%-12% of NAV (maximum 15%) and typical high conviction short equity positions are sized at 3%-4% of NAV (maximum 7.5%).
Initial position sizes are usually 3% of NAV for the longs and 1% of NAV for the shorts; as conviction grows, positions are scaled-up. Potential catalysts can be an input to sizing decisions. The sum of long positions sized >5% is likely to exceed 80% of NAV at most times. The portfolio is likely to be composed of 15-25 longs and 10-15 shorts (excluding hedges). 

Gross equity exposure range: 100% to 200%. Net equity exposure range: from net short up to 100% net long. 
Typical net equity exposure in the +40% to +70% band. Opportunistic gross credit exposure range: 0% to 50%.

results.name: Chenavari European Debt Opportunities IV
results.management_company_description:
Chenavari is an established, credit-focused asset manager with a core expertise in European markets. With expertise across the liquidity spectrum of credit, Chenavari aims to profit from idiosyncrasies and inefficiencies within credit markets, which are due to macro (such as banks' deleveraging, monetary policies, etc.) as well as technical factors. The Firm concentrates its investment activity on fundamental strategies that may offer attractive risk-reward profiles on a relative value basis with low market correlation and low beta to broad credit markets.

Chenavari’s investment strategies can be segmented across three groups: 

•	Liquid strategies, including investments in single name corporates, European financials, credit indices, asset-backed securities, across both cash and derivative markets;
•	Private Credit strategies, such as portfolio acquisitions of primarily performing loans; risk sharing/significant risk transfer, asset-based lending, and specialty finance (new loan origination) in consumer finance, receivables and leasing; and
•	CLO management, including investment in senior secured loans and revolving credit facilities through European collateralised loan obligation structures.
results.strategy_description:
The Fund seeks to deliver attractive risk adjusted returns and stable income by investing in granular, predominantly performing European loan portfolios through two complementary sub-strategies: Specialty Finance (Credit Origination and Portfolio Acquisitions) and Significant Risk Transfer (SRT) transactions. Underlying exposures may include large corporate, SME, trade finance, asset backed, and secured and unsecured consumer loans.

The Fund operates an institutional evergreen structure allowing continuous subscriptions and defined liquidity windows, enabling investors to adjust their exposure over time via a structured pass-through share class mechanism.

results.name: Otter Rock Advisors Fund
results.management_company_description:
Otter Rock is a global, fundamental equity long/short fund focused on TMT, fintech, consumer and industrials impacted by technological change. The portfolio will run mid-net through-cycle, while maintaining a concentrated, factor aware, but not factor constrained portfolio with significant exposure to small and mid-cap equities on the long and short side. The firm is committed to building a robust short book of single name alpha-generative ideas. 

Otter Rock is led by CIO Alix Karlan who brings over 10 years of investment experience and 18 years of entrepreneurial experience to the firm.  Otter Rock is the culmination of Karlan’s professional experiences. By leveraging his learnings from both Viking and Alua, Karlan will bring to bear the risk management, capital allocation and talent development approach he learned at Viking to a concentrated portfolio strategy he has developed with his own capital since departing Alua.  At first, the CIO will manage capital allocation and portfolio oversight entirely. Over time, we plan to cultivate internal sector leaders to act as discretionary portfolio managers much in the way Viking developed their sub portfolios, the structure of which Karlan helped revamp while there. We believe our sub-portfolios will allow sector experts to express their top ideas while also learning to manage a concentrated L/S, alpha-generating portfolio. The CIO's portfolio we believe will utilize insights from the sub-PMs to maintain focus on our best ideas. This approach we believe will benefit our investors by fostering firm-wide confidence in our top ideas, enhancing talent development, creating a performance focused culture while ensuring team continuity, and by developing the next generation of leaders so that Otter Rock endures to serve investors for the long term.
